source.title: Towards Unifying Interpretability and Control: Evaluation via Intervention
source.authors: Usha Bhalla; Suraj Srinivas; Asma Ghandeharioun; Himabindu Lakkaraju

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates interventions using SAE features and measures SAE reconstruction error, but it does not test whether SAE error is structured, predictable from the input, or shared across SAE sizes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports normalized latent reconstruction errors for SAEs and describes coherence after replacing activations with SAE reconstructions. These results do not measure the error’s structure or predictability, compare errors across SAE sizes or tokens, compare SAE errors with matched random errors, or test error’s role in circuits or steering. The paper’s statements about feature-label noise and reconstruction error are its own observations, not tests of the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study benchmarks interpretability methods (lens, SAE, probes, steering) for intervention success and coherence. It reports SAE reconstruction error magnitudes and coherence after reconstruction only as sanity checks. It does not test error predictability, scaling across SAE sizes, loss impact versus matched random errors, linear/nonlinear error decomposition, or whether keeping the error term preserves behaviour. It does not cite or engage the dark-matter paper; it only notes that SAE reconstruction 'incurs a significant error'. 'cites_only' is the closest fit: it neither tests nor uses the claim. 'discusses' would overstate its engagement.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but misses the main conclusion. The authors conclude that interpretability methods allow intervention but inconsistently. Lens methods beat SAEs and probes on simple features, and all methods trade off coherence and underperform prompting. They attribute weak SAE steering mainly to noisy feature labels. Reconstruction error is a sanity-check side note.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses SAE feature reconstruction and evaluates interventions and output quality; it does not apply the original study’s measurements of error predictability, per-token scaling, or cross-size error overlap.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction error varies across the reported models; the paper does not test how its structure varies with SAE size.

fits_no_version.finding: Normalized SAE reconstruction error is 0.38 (Gemma2-2b L20) and 1.64 (GPT2-small L9). Outputs generated from SAE-reconstructed activations keep roughly clean-level coherence. SAE reconstruction makes the minimal intervention edit distance nonzero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Off-the-shelf SAE reconstruction error magnitudes vary greatly across models, while text generated from the reconstructions stays roughly as coherent as clean text under an LLM judge.

record.problems: The reconstruction-error results do not include uncertainty estimates or matched random-error controls. Reconstruction errors are not tested across SAE sizes or decomposed into predictable and nonlinear parts. Coherence results for SAE reconstruction are shown in a figure without model-specific numerical values in the text.

untested.parts: All: no linear prediction of the error from the input.
All: no per-token norms, no cross-size comparison, no scaling.
All: no comparison of loss against same-norm random errors.
All: no decomposition into linear and nonlinear parts.
All: no steering or circuit analysis with versus without the error term. SAE interventions decode the full reconstruction and drop the error, but this is never compared.
All: no comparison of architectures or training objectives.

record.verdict_notes: The paper does not engage the SAE error-structure claim. Its SAE results concern steering fidelity via feature labels, not dark matter.

versions.untested_parts: No test of whether SAE error is linearly predictable from the input activation.
No per-token error norm analysis, cross-size predictability or context-overlap comparison, or test of whether error vanishes with SAE scale.
No comparison of model loss after SAE reconstruction against random errors of the same size.
No separation of linear and nonlinear error components or test of their feature-learning properties.
No test of whether circuits, steering, or other analyses lose behavior when the SAE error term is omitted. Coherence after reconstruction alone does not measure that claim.
No comparison of SAE training objectives or architectures, or test of whether improved training makes the error shrink.

rows.subject: Gemma2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Measured normalized latent reconstruction error when the activation was reconstructed from SAE features without intervention.
rows.note: This is a reconstruction-error magnitude, not a measurement of the error’s structure, predictability, or behavior across SAE sizes.
rows.check: A single error magnitude (0.38, Gemma Scope L20) with no structure, size or random-error comparison. It is a sanity-check value, not a test of any version.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Measured normalized latent reconstruction error when the activation was reconstructed from SAE features without intervention.
rows.note: This is a reconstruction-error magnitude, not a measurement of the error’s structure, predictability, or behavior across SAE sizes.
rows.check: A single error magnitude (1.64, GPT2-small L9 SAELens SAE). This normalized error exceeds 1, which suggests a possible SAE or setup issue the authors don't explain. It bears on no version.

rows.subject: SAE reconstructions (GPT2-small and Gemma2-2b)
rows.operation_detail: Compared output coherence after replacing the activation with its SAE reconstruction, without an intervention, against clean model outputs.
rows.note: The authors state that reconstructed-latent outputs generally match clean-output coherence, but do not provide model-specific numerical values in the text. Coherence does not test the listed error-structure claims.
rows.check: Figure 7 shows coherence after replacement for SAEs only on GPT2-sm and Gemma2-2b. It gives no loss measure and no random-error control, so it cannot speak to V3. The authors state coherence 'generally matches' clean outputs.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
